sentences.text:
R.DEVDAS J., (ORAL):
The petitioners are aggrieved of the impugned order dated 08.05.2019 at Annexure 'M' passed by the second respondent-Deputy Commissioner, Bengaluru Urban District, in Revision Petn. No.417/2014-15.
2.

At the outset, the learned Senior Counsel Sri G.Krishnamurthy, appearing on behalf of the petitioners would submit that the revision petition was filed by Sri V.Nanjappa, who was aggrieved of the order passed by the Assistant Commissioner, Bengaluru North Sub-Division in R.A.No.(BN)15/2013-14.

The fifth respondent had filed an appeal before the Assistant Commissioner invoking NC: 2024:KHC:1771 Section 136(2) of the Karnataka Land Revenue Act,
1964, seeking to set aside an order passed by the Tahsildar on 15.04.2011 directing restoration of the name of Sri V.Nanjappa, in the land records in respect of Sy.No.35/7, measuring 35 guntas and Sy.No.35/8, measuring 1 acre 15 guntas situated at Nagavara Village, Kasaba Hobli, Bangalore North Taluk.
In brief, it is submitted that Sri V.Nanjappa, was the owner of the said lands.
The said lands were notified and acquired for the purpose of formation of a residential layout for the benefit of the members of Vyalikaval House Building Co-operative Society.

It is submitted that the acquisition proceedings were challenged by several of the land owners and ultimately the Hon'ble Supreme Court declared that the entire acquisition proceedings were void and therefore directed that the lands have to be restored back to the owners along with certain conditions regarding re-deposit of the compensation amount wherever the owners had received the compensation.

The learned Senior Counsel has taken this Court through some of the material available on record to show that Sri V.Nanjappa, had returned the amount that he had received as compensation from the Special Land Acquisition Officer.
Thereafter Sri V.Najappa approached the Tahsildar to restore his name in the land records.
Pursuant to the same, orders were passed by the Tahsildar ordering restoration of the name of Sri V.Nanjappa in the land records.
Nevertheless, the Assistant Commissioner entertained an appeal filed at the hands of the fifth respondent and passed an order on 15.12.2014 at Annexure 'F' setting aside the order of the Tahsildar.

Being aggrieved, Sri V.Nanjappa, approached the Deputy Commissioner in R.P.No.417/2014-15.
4.

Learned Senior Counsel takes this Court through the order sheet maintained by the Deputy Commissioner and submits that on several occasions there were no sittings of the Deputy V. Nanjappa vs State Of Karnataka on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198013276/

sentences.text: Commissioner.

However, on 26.10.2018 it was noticed that since the revisional petitioner V.Nanjappa, had died and a memo in that NC: 2024:KHC:1771 regard was filed, however, even after noticing the same it was directed that the matter is reserved for final orders.
On the other hand, an application under Order XXII Rule 3 read with Section 151 of CPC was filed on 22.08.2016 itself which was not noticed by the Deputy Commissioner.

entities.text: Order XXII Rule 3 read with Section 151
entities.label: PROVISION

sentences.text: No orders were passed on the application to bring the legal representatives on record.
As a consequence of which, without hearing the parties on the merits of the matter, the impugned order has been passed by the Deputy Commissioner against a dead person.

In that view of the matter, the learned Senior Counsel would submit that the matter requires reconsideration at the hands of the Deputy Commissioner after bringing the legal representatives on record and hearing the parties on merits.

5. Having regard to the submission made by the learned Senior Counsel and on perusing the petition papers, it is clear that the application filed by the petitioners herein to bring themselves on record as legal representatives of Sri V.Nanjappa, was never heard or allowed by the Deputy Commissioner.

Consequently, it NC: 2024:KHC:1771 has to be held that the impugned order has been passed against a dead person.
6.
Consequently, the writ petition is allowed.
The impugned order dated 08.05.2019 passed by the Deputy Commissioner, Bengaluru Urban District at Annexure 'M' is hereby quashed and set aside.

The matter is remitted back to the Deputy Commissioner, to enable the petitioners herein to get an order in respect of an application already filed on 22.08.2016 which has been produced at Annexure 'J'.
The Deputy Commissioner shall consider the application, permit the petitioners to come on record and thereafter consider the matter on merits after hearing both the sides.
Ordered accordingly.

Sd/-
JUDGE JT/-
